# Forensic-feature fixtures

Normal tests are offline. External tools/native APIs below are development
oracles only and never participate in production parsing.

`sources.json` records uncompressed hashes and lengths generated by
`tools/generate_forensic_fixtures.py`. The underlying NTFS image is the existing
[dfVFS fixture](../layers/README.md); the [dfVFS license](../LICENSE.dfvfs)
applies to that source and its derivatives.

- `windows.lznt1`, `windows-variable.lznt1`: Windows `RtlCompressBuffer`, with
  output independently reread by `RtlDecompressBuffer`. Matching source bytes
  are committed; the variable-pattern fixture exercises changing token widths.
- `windows.sd`: Windows
  `ConvertStringSecurityDescriptorToSecurityDescriptorW` output for the SDDL
  recorded in the manifest. Includes owner/group, deny/allow DACL ACEs and SACL.
- `ntfs-forensics.raw`: specified NTFS attribute/runlist changes wrapping the
  Windows-compressed bytes; compressed, fragmented, raw, sparse and short final
  units. `ntfs-deleted.raw` adds resident/free/reallocated candidate records.
- `ntfs-journal-security.raw`: shared `$Secure:$SDS`, sparse `$UsnJrnl:$J` with
  specified records/`$Max`, and two specified LFS restart pages. These journal
  structures are constructed test fixtures, not captured Windows journal output.
- `tsk-forensic-reference.json`: TSK 4.15.0 independently extracted record 66
  (compressed stream) and record 27 (deleted resident data), matching known source
  bytes. The compressed source SHA-256 is
  `fa2b0dab0059102e78ca7ec110c17c8db6bb3c29abe049e75bf85f75f53d5cdd`.
- `ntfs-forensics.E01`: libewf EnCase 6 profile wrapping the journal/security
  fixture. `bitlocker-mbr.E01`: MBR with an encrypted XTS test volume at LBA 2048.
  Libewf independently reread each wrapper to the exact source bytes.

`bitlocker-generated.json` records six v2 BitLocker containers generated with
OpenSSL-backed cryptography 50.0.2 in `tools/generate_bitlocker_fixtures.py`.
They cover all six software encryption method IDs 0x8000–0x8005. Cryptography
provides independent AES-CBC, AES-XTS and AES-CCM; the published Elephant diffuser
equations are implemented separately in the Python writer. The original NTFS
plaintext is known; decoded hashes account for zeroed metadata/backup-header
virtual ranges. Public fixture keys, VMK, user password and recovery password
are recorded in the manifest. They are **test data, not user credentials**.

`bdetogo-selected.raw.gz` preserves selected original encrypted sectors of the
[dfVFS Windows-written BitLocker To Go image](https://github.com/log2timeline/dfvfs/blob/d365f334da42169276e2083a27f75bc2afa48ea8/test_data/bdetogo.raw).
Original SHA-256:
`ed7982a1f9263e4e54889fea1fa74112d12fea0a0aa7cd8f84fc6f03198ae71b`;
Git blob ID `8480a3f28ef9a3b74c8544def6687899a15d8e59`.
The public password is `bde-TEST`, as published in dfVFS tests. Unlocking and
known-file extraction were validated on the complete 67,108,864-byte original
before selection. The selected
fixture keeps boot/metadata, FAT/root and known `passwords.txt` sectors; all other
bytes are replaced with zeros to avoid storing ~62 MiB of unrelated ciphertext.
**It is not a complete original image and must not be used as a whole-image
decryption golden.** Exact retained ranges, selected-image hash and the source
URL are in `bdetogo-selection.json`. `tools/select_bitlocker_fixture.py` uses
independent OpenSSL key authentication, diffuser/CBC and FAT parsing to verify
the selected known file against its pre-existing dfVFS SHA-256.

Primary references:

- [Microsoft LZNT1 algorithm](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-xca/5655f4a3-6ba4-489b-959f-e1f407c52f15)
- [Microsoft security descriptor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-security_descriptor_relative)
- [Microsoft USN v2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winioctl/ns-winioctl-usn_record_v2), [v3](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winioctl/ns-winioctl-usn_record_v3), [v4](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winioctl/ns-winioctl-usn_record_v4)
- [libyal NTFS format](https://github.com/libyal/libfsntfs/blob/main/documentation/New%20Technologies%20File%20System%20(NTFS).asciidoc)
- [libyal BitLocker format](https://github.com/libyal/libbde/blob/main/documentation/BitLocker%20Drive%20Encryption%20(BDE)%20format.asciidoc)

Reproduction:

```powershell
python tools/generate_forensic_fixtures.py
python tools/generate_bitlocker_fixtures.py
python tools/validate_forensic_tsk.py --tsk-bin target/tsk-oracle/sleuthkit-4.15.0-win32/bin --libewf D:/Projects/autopsy/thirdparty/ewfexport_exec/64-bit/libewf.dll --generate
```

The first script needs Windows. The crypto generator needs cryptography in the
isolated `target/crypto-oracle` directory. To reproduce the public selection,
download the pinned original to `tests/fixtures/forensics/bdetogo.raw.gz` after
checking its hash, then run `tools/select_bitlocker_fixture.py`; it moves the
unmodified full download into `target/bdetogo-original.raw.gz`.
